name: 2.2 Histograms and Frequency Tables
_note:
Ten of the original sixteen slots are questions the bank already had -- 2.2's first five problems are frequency-table work 1.3 covers outright, and its "at most three T-shirts" multiple choice is cumulative-relative-frequency-at-most almost word for word. Reused questions are marked; they are attached by qsetid, never copied, so a later fix improves every section using them. The original four new ones cover what nothing in the bank did: what the frequency columns sum to and why, what changes when bin width doubles, comparing two groups of different sizes, and grouping raw data into stated classes before answering. (2) The one histogram-family question with continuous class boundaries (0.5-6.5 style survival-day cutoffs) was swapped for complete-grouped-frequency-table-discrete.php, a like-for-like replacement with the same three-part shape (missing frequency, relative frequency, cumulative relative frequency of a named class) but whole-number classes (0-5, 6-11, ... 30-35); the bank had no existing 2.1/2.2-appropriate discrete-bin grouped-frequency-table question to reuse instead (checked question-index.json, family descriptive-stats and displays; grouped-interval-boundary-select-all.php teaches fractional boundaries on purpose and would contradict a discrete swap). questions.title: What the Frequency Columns Sum To - State the totals of the frequency and relative frequency columns of a survey table, then separate what frequency, relative frequency and cumulative relative frequency each measure
Back-Solve Frequency from Cumulative Relative Frequency - Recover a missing frequency from a known cumulative relative frequency, then complete the relative and cumulative columns and find percents

Diagnose a Cumulative-vs-Individual Percent Claim - Catch a published claim that reports a row's cumulative relative frequency as if it were that row's own relative frequency, then compute the row's true percent

Cumulative Relative Frequency "At Most" from Hurricane Table - Given a frequency table of hurricane direct hits by category (1-5), compute the cumulative relative frequency of storms at most category 3

Percent More Than a Cutoff via the Complement Rule - Find the percent above a cutoff as 1 minus the cumulative relative frequency through the cutoff row, then confirm it by adding the relative frequencies of the rows above the cutoff

Complete a Grouped Frequency Table with Discrete Classes - given a grouped table of whole-number counts with one frequency missing, find that frequency and the relative and cumulative relative frequencies of a named class

Grouped Frequency Table and Graphs - Read frequencies, relative frequencies, and cumulative relative frequencies from a grouped frequency table of CEO ages, and identify which graph shape corresponds to each type
Histogram - Relative Frequency and Shape - Read a class count off a drawn histogram, turn it into a relative frequency, and identify the shape of the distribution

Bin Width Changes the Picture - One data set is drawn as a histogram twice, with bars one unit wide and then two units wide; count the wider bars, work out the height of one of them, and say what the change of bin width does and does not alter

Compare Two Groups of Different Sizes - Two relative frequency histograms drawn from surveys with different sample sizes; read one class's share, decide which group spends more, and say why raw counts cannot be compared here

Classes and Shape from a Raw Data Set - Group a randomized data set into classes of a stated width, then report a class count, where the tallest class starts, a relative frequency and the shape of the distribution

Build the Grouped Frequency Table for a Histogram - Sort twenty raw measurements into five given classes, enter each class frequency and the total, then say why the bars of a histogram touch while a bar graph leaves gaps

Pre-FRQ Grade a Display Choice - The scenario and grading checklist of a histogram-vs-bar-graph FRQ (rewritten from a histogram-vs-box-plot scenario, which is 2.4 content), but the student grades four sample responses against the rubric instead of writing one
Find the Class Width - Compute a data set's range and the whole-number class width needed to cover it in a stated number of classes, then say why the width is rounded up
Label the Bins from a Class Width - Fill in the missing class boundary labels of a partly-completed grouped frequency table, then say which class a boundary-sitting value belongs to and why
